name: hey
readmeExcerpt:
hey is a tiny program that sends some load to a web application.

hey was originally called boom and was influenced from Tarek Ziade's
tool at [tarekziade/boom](https://github.com/tarekziade/boom). Using the same name was a mistake as it resulted in cases
where binary name conflicts created confusion.
To preserve the name for its original owner, we renamed this project to hey.

## Installation

  - Linux (amd64): https://storage.googleapis.com/hey-releases/hey_linux_amd64
  - macOS (amd64): https://storage.googleapis.com/hey-releases/hey_darwin_amd64
  - Windows (amd64): https://storage.googleapis.com/hey-releases/hey_windows_amd64

### Package Managers

macOS:
-  [Homebrew](https://brew.sh/) users can use `brew install hey`.

## Usage

hey runs provided number of requests in the provided concurrency level and prints stats.

It also supports HTTP2 endpoints.

```
Usage: hey [options...] <url>

Options:
  -n  Number of requests to run. Default is 200.
  -c  Number of workers to run concurrently. Total number of requests cannot
      be smaller than the concurrency level. Default is 50.
  -q  Rate limit, in queries per second (QPS) per worker. Default is no rate limit.
  -z  Duration of application to send requests. When duration is reached,
      application stops and exits. If duration is specified, n is ignored.
      Examples: -z 10s -z 3m.
  -o  Output type. If none provided, a summary is printed.
      "csv" is the only supported alternative. Dumps the response
      metrics in comma-separated values format.

  -m  HTTP method, one of GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS.
  -H  Custom HTTP header. You can specify as many as needed by repeating the flag.
      For example, -H "Accept: text/html" -H "Content-Type: application/xml" .
  -t  Timeout for each request in seconds. Default is 20, use 0 for infinite.
  -A  HTTP Accept header.
  -d  HTTP request body.
  -D  HTTP request body from file. For example, /home/user/file.txt or ./file.txt.
  -T  Content-type, defaults to "text/html".
  -a  Basic authentication, username:password.
  -x  HTTP Proxy address as host:port.
  -h2 Enable HTTP/2.

  -host	HTTP Host header.

  -disable-compression  Disable compression.
  -disable-keepalive    Disable keep-alive, prevents re-use of TCP
                        connections between different HTTP requests.
  -disable-redirects    Disable following of HTTP redirects
  -cpus                 Number of used cpu cores.
                        (default for current machine is 8 cores)
```

## Examples

Make requests with default settings:
```
hey https://google.com
```

Make 1000 requests with 100 concurrent workers:
```
hey -n 1000 -c 100 https://google.com
```

Run load test for 30 seconds:
```
hey -z 30s https://google.com
```

Make POST request with custom body:
```
hey \
    -m POST \
    -d "param1=value1&param2=value2" \
    https://google.com
```

Add custom headers:
```
hey \
    -H "Accept: application/json" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer token" \
    https://google.com
```

Test with HTTP/2:
```
hey -h2 https://google.com
```

Rate limit to 10 queries per second per worker:
```
hey -q 10 -c 5 -z 30s https://google.com
```

## What's Changed
* Added Dockerfile by @jnovack in https://github.com/rakyll/hey/pull/226
* Fix DNS dialup detailed output in print.go by @tstraley in https://github.com/rakyll/hey/pull/207
* Upgrade deps by @chenrui333 in https://github.com/rakyll/hey/pull/178
* Updated User-Agent header logic by @phriscage in https://github.com/rakyll/hey/pull/87
* Introduce CI with GitHub Actions by @rakyll in https://github.com/rakyll/hey/pull/332

## New Contributors

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/rakyll/hey/compare/v0.1.4...v0.1.5

aiSummary.oneLiner: Tiny, highly concurrent HTTP load generator and ApacheBench replacement.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Hey is a command-line tool written in Go that generates HTTP load against web applications. It serves as a modern, cross-platform replacement for ApacheBench (ab). It allows developers to easily test the concurrency and performance of their endpoints by sending a specified number of requests with configurable concurrency levels. It outputs detailed statistics on response times, status codes, and latency distributions.
keyFeatures: High concurrency: leverages Go's goroutines to simulate massive parallel HTTP requests efficiently.
Cross-platform binaries: available as a single executable for Linux, macOS, and Windows.
Detailed analytics: outputs comprehensive metrics including latency histograms and percentile distributions.
Customizable requests: supports custom HTTP headers, methods, and payload bodies for varied testing.
ApacheBench alternative: provides a simpler, more robust modern replacement for the traditional ab tool.

useCases.title: Benchmark web servers
useCases.description: Send thousands of concurrent requests to evaluate the maximum throughput of an API endpoint.

useCases.title: Test load balancers
useCases.description: Simulate heavy traffic spikes to verify that load balancing configurations distribute traffic correctly.

useCases.title: Analyze latency percentiles
useCases.description: Measure the 95th and 99th percentile response times to identify tail latency issues.

useCases.title: Stress test microservices
useCases.description: Automate load generation in CI/CD pipelines to ensure performance regressions do not occur.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Backend developers, DevOps engineers, and QA testers needing a lightweight, fast tool to benchmark HTTP services.
